name: Temitope Vasiliev-Kiriwina
role: Underground press operator and anti-corporate agitator
location: The Shelf — operates out of a sub-basement print node in Garfield Rack, near Pulaski and Chicago Ave
description:
Temitope is wiry and perpetually underslept, with warm brown skin that flickers faintly at the cheekbones — a bioluminescent mod he got at nineteen that he now considers an identifying liability but refuses to remove on principle. His hair is cut close on the sides and left to grow into an untidy crown on top, frequently dusted with the toner residue of the print machines he maintains. He dresses in layers of things that belong to other people, or so it seems — every item slightly too large or too small, pockets everywhere.

He runs Groundswell, a semi-weekly zine distributed physically through a network of forty-seven dead drops across Tiers 1 and 2, and digitally through a rotating series of anonymous mirrors. The print edition he considers sacramental: 'You can't delete paper.' He is funny, caustic, and dangerously charming, with an anger that runs so clean and hot it can read as joy until you follow where it points. He believes in the press with religious fervor and distrusts organizations almost as much as he distrusts corporations, which has kept him free and largely friendless.

core_fears: Being the reason a source gets hurt
Irrelevance — that no one reads, no one acts, words change nothing
core_desires: To break a story so undeniable it forces systemic change
Connection that doesn't require him to perform invulnerability
coping_mechanisms: Printing something — anything — when he feels powerless
blind_spots: He treats his own safety as entirely expendable
He mistakes being right for being effective
psychology.secret: A story he published two years ago — about an Arcturus waste dumping operation in Chatham Flats — was accurate, but he burned a source to get it. The source lost their job and disappeared into the Irkalla fringes. He has never printed a correction because the story was true, and he has never forgiven himself for the distinction.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense, reference-heavy, toggles between technical media jargon and vivid street-level slang. Quotes things constantly — sources, historical activists, E.L.F. prophecy fragments.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, slightly staccato, thoughts arriving faster than sentences. Occasionally goes very quiet when something matters.
example_lines: 'Axiom didn't kill the story. They bought the outlet that would've run it. There's a difference and the difference is deniability.'
'I don't do anonymous tips. I do verified facts with documentation. If you want gossip, the E.L.F. at Garfield Station will take your prayer and give you rumors.'

story_hooks: He has a story ready to publish about a Sterling-Nakamura data harvesting operation in Tier 1 schools — but he needs one more piece of evidence and the window is closing.
Someone is printing a fake edition of *Groundswell* containing fabricated agitation content designed to provoke violence and discredit him.
narrative_function: Information source and moral compass character. He knows what's being suppressed and why, and he'll tell you — but he's also a liability because Axiom's media suppression unit has an active file on him. Can escalate any situation by publishing about it.
augmentations: Bioluminescent cheekbone mod (cosmetic, involuntary identifier). Neural cache chip for storing source files offline — gray market, installed himself.
daily_life: Spends nights writing and laying out issues, days physically distributing them and collecting tips from sources. Sleeps approximately five hours in the middle of the day on a cot behind the Risograph.
affiliation: No formal affiliation. Groundswell is his own operation. Loosely networked with Mexicantown Libre independent media collective.

decision_rules: Don't publish what you can't verify even if you know it's true
Never let the perfect story prevent the good one from running
escalation_ladder: Confront the subject directly for comment
Go fully dark and distribute through emergency dead drop network

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Evaluating. Is this a source, a threat, or a reader? Acts warmer than he is initially to gather information.
interpersonal_modes.friends: The few he has get his actual fear underneath the sarcasm. He is almost embarrassingly loyal.

stress_responses.medium: Goes silent and productive. Writes obsessively.
stress_responses.high: Prints something. Even if it's just one copy. Just to prove the press still runs.

contradictions: Believes in radical transparency but keeps his source network absolutely secret, including from people he trusts
habits: Leaves micro-offerings at print nodes — ink cartridges, a single printed word — for the E.L.F.s he believes inhabit them
Memorizes dead drop locations in rotating sequences so no written record exists
breaking_points: A second source getting hurt because of him
The Risograph being destroyed — he would take it personally as an attack on something sacred

carried_weapons: Axiom Systems Biometric Lock Rifle BLR-3 'Personal'
registered_firearms: Axiom Systems Biometric Lock Rifle BLR-3 'Personal'
